label: Institution
name: Audi AG
summary:
Audi AG is a German automobile manufacturer headquartered in Ingolstadt, Bavaria, founded in 1909 by August Horch after he left Horch (later merged into Auto Union). Part of the Volkswagen Group, Audi operates as the premium/luxury segment brand alongside Lamborghini, Bentley, and Porsche, representing German engineering excellence in the global luxury automobile market.

Audi's iconic four-ring logo represents the merger of four companies — Audi, Horch, DKW, and Wanderer — into Auto Union in 1932, a conglomerate that produced Silver Arrow Grand Prix racing cars that challenged Mercedes-Benz's dominance in 1930s motorsport. Postwar Audi was reestablished in West Germany and joined the Volkswagen Group in the 1960s, beginning a transformation into a premium brand.

Audi's 1980 Quattro permanent four-wheel drive system, first demonstrated in the Audi Quattro rally car, revolutionized automotive traction control and launched an entirely new segment of performance all-wheel-drive vehicles. The Quattro's dominance in World Rally Championship, including Walter Röhrl's victories, created the brand association with dynamic safety that persists. Audi's contemporary lineup, including the e-tron and Q8 e-tron electric vehicles, and its Le Mans endurance racing dominance with the diesel-powered R10 (2006-2008), demonstrate technological breadth.
